region.text: the khanate's territory under the Manghit ataliqs

ledger.note: 1785: Shah Murad founds the Emirate of Bukhara. 'The emirate was officially created in 1785, upon the assumption of rulership by the Manghit emir, Shah Murad'; the Khanate of Bukhara page: 'In 1785, his descendant, Shah Murad, formalized the family's dynastic rule' and used the title emir because the Manghits were non-Chingissid.
1785: Shah Murad attacks Merv. 'In 1785, the Manghit amir of Bukhara, Shah Murad, attacked the city and killed the ruler, Bayram 'Ali Khan Qajar.'
1789: Merv is razed. 'In 1788 and 1789, Shah Murad razed the city to the ground, and broke down the dams.' Cliopatria gives the oasis to Bukhara from 1791.

region.text: the Merv oasis and the Murghab

ledger.note: 1789: the Merv oasis passes to Bukhara. The page says Shah Murad razed the city in 1788-89 and gives no formal annexation; Cliopatria's Bukhara shape holds the oasis from 1791 and Mary 73% from 1800 (the upper Murghab is not dated by any opened page).
1823: Merv goes to Khiva. 'Merv passed to the Khanate of Khiva in 1823' (the Khiva dossier: 'Muhammad Rahim I conquered the city of Merv'); Cliopatria's Bukhara shape drops it in 1822.

region.text: Jizzakh and Ura-Tepe, the Zarafshan approaches

ledger.note: 1866: the Russian war. 'Romanovsky prepared to attack Bohkara, the Amir moved first, the two forces met on the plain of Irjar'; no day on the page.
1866: Ura-Tepe and Jizzakh fall. 'Then he moved west and took Ura-Tepe' and 'Jizzakh from Bukhara'; Romanovsky then took Khujand from Kokand. Cliopatria drops the lands in 1864.

May 1868: Samarkand surrenders. 'The city surrendered without resisting (May 1868)'; 'the Emirate of Bukhara lost Samarkand and remained a semi-independent vassal' until the Russian Revolution. The Emirate page: Russia 'annexed much of the emirate's territory, including the important city of Samarkand'.

5 July 1868: the peace treaty. 'On 2 June 1868, in a decisive battle on the Zerabulak heights, the Russians defeated the main forces of the Emir' and 'on 5 July 1868, a peace treaty was signed.' The Emirate becomes a Russian vassal (1868 on this page; 'In 1873, the remainder became a Russian protectorate' on the Emirate page).

c. 1870: Shahrisabz. The 1916 list of the emirate's begliks gives 'Shahrisabz (c 1870, now Kashkadarya Region)'; Cliopatria's shape holds Qashqadaryo (91-100%) from 1788, the Khanate page has Rahim Bi subjugating Shahr-i Sabz in 1753, so the shape and the list disagree.

c. 1878: Darvaz. The 1916 list gives 'Darvaz (c 1878, now Darvoz district, Tajikistan)'; 'The Pamirs were under Bukharan rule from the late 19th century'. Cliopatria's shape holds Gorno-Badakhshan from 1788.

28 August 1920: the Red Army attacks Bukhara. 'On 28 August 1920, an army of well-disciplined and well equipped Red Army troops under the command of Bolshevik general Mikhail Frunze attacked the city of Bukhara.' The emir fled on 31 August to Dushanbe in Eastern Bukhara.
2 September 1920: 'after four days of fighting, the emir's citadel (the Ark) was destroyed.'

2 September 1920: the Emirate falls. 'The Emirate of Bukhara was conquered by the Bolsheviks and replaced with the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic', proclaimed on 8 October 1920 under Fayzulla Khodzhayev; the Emirate page gives the dissolution as 2 September 1920 ('Fall of Bukhara').

wars.name: Shah Murad's conquest of Merv
wars.outcome: Shah Murad killed Bayram 'Ali Khan Qajar in 1785 and razed Merv and its dams in 1788-89; the oasis was Bukharan until 1823.

wars.name: Bukharan-Afghan crisis on the Amu Darya (1788)
wars.outcome: Timur Shah's page: Shah Murad 'crossed the Amu Darya in the summer of 1788' after Timur Shah failed to recall his governors of Aqcha and Balkh; the page gives no result. The Amu Darya remained the frontier (Durrani Empire page).
wars.note: No territorial event recorded; the page is silent on the outcome.

wars.name: Khivan conquest of Merv (1823)
wars.outcome: Merv passed from Bukhara to Khiva in 1823.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Bukhara (1866-1868)

zones.text: Jizzakh, Ura-Tepe, Samarkand and the Zarafshan

wars.outcome: Russian victories at Irjar (1866), Ura-Tepe and Jizzakh (1866) and Zerabulak (2 June 1868); Samarkand lost in May 1868; peace treaty 5 July 1868; the remainder a vassal and, on the Emirate page, a protectorate from 1873.

wars.name: Bukhara Operation (Red Army, 1920)
wars.outcome: Frunze's attack of 28 August 1920 destroyed the Ark on 2 September; the emir fled to Dushanbe on 31 August and later to Kabul; the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was proclaimed on 8 October 1920.

certainty.note: Desert, steppe and mountain frontiers with Khiva, Kokand and the Afghan khanates were approximate; the Amu Darya line with the Afghans is a river line.

Sharp from the Russian frontier fixed after the treaty of 5 July 1868 (and the 1873 protectorate) and the Amu Darya line fixed by the Russian-Afghan demarcation of 1886 and 1893 (Russian conquest page); the Pamir edge stays soft.

notes: Cliopatria's Emirate of Bukhara row has a 50-year hole: shapes 1788-1867 and 1918-1919, nothing for 1868-1917 although the emirate lasted to 2 September 1920 as a vassal (1868) or protectorate (1873) of Russia; a new keyframe (emirate-of-bukhara_1868) fills 1868-1917 from the 1918 shape. The relation to Russia belongs in the russian-empire ledger as vassal_start for emirate-of-bukhara: the Russian conquest page dates it 5 July 1868 ('remained a semi-independent vassal'), the Emirate page 1873 ('quasi-independent Russian protectorate (1873-1920)'). Corrections made: the Pamirs (Gorno-Badakhshan) are taken out of the 1788-1863 shapes (page: Darvaz c 1878, Pamirs late 19th century), and the 1864 shape is replaced by the 1863 outline because Cliopatria drops Samarkand, Jizzakh and Ura-Tyube four years before the Russians took them (1866 and May 1868). Not settled with the five pages: the date of the Pamirs (Shughnan, Roshan) and how long Bukhara held them; the Khiva strip given to Bukhara in October 1873 (the Khiva dossier carries it as a loss to emirate-of-bukhara; this dossier has no page for it); the fighting with Kokand over Ura-Tyube from 1788 and Bukhara's occupation of Kokand in June-August 1842 (the Kokand dossier carries them; this dossier did not open the Kokand page, so the mirror events are missing here); the Chahar Wilayat's nominal Bukharan suzerainty in the first half of the 19th century (Emirate page, undated); Cliopatria's constant 1809-1863 shape against Nasrullah's 30 begliks. Page conflicts: Shah Murad's reign 1785-1800 (table) against 1785-1799 (infobox); the Khanate page flags conflicting dates throughout; the Red Army's failed assault is March 1920 on the Emirate page and March 1918 on the republic page; the Merv page has Khiva taking Merv in 1823, Cliopatria drops it in 1822. The Emirate page gives no area; the republic page's 182,193 km2 is the only check. Counterparts needing dossiers: bukharan-people-s-soviet-republic (1920-1924, Cliopatria lacks it), Merv under its Qajar governors (to 1785) and the Shahrisabz begs. Page budget: 5 pages were opened for this state (Emirate of Bukhara, Russian conquest of Central Asia, Khanate of Bukhara, Merv, Bukharan People's Soviet Republic); the Timur Shah, Ahmad Shah and Emirate of Afghanistan pages were opened for neighbouring dossiers and are reused. Gazetteer: used 'Gorno-Badakhshan', 'Mary', 'Jizzakh', 'Samarkand' as found; Istaravshan is the place name for Ura-Tepe.
